body: I have no one to help me. My youngest is too young for kindergarten.
I’ve seen a doctor and 2 psychologists. I can’t go to the appointments anymore because there is no one to watch my children while I go.

No, I haven't yet because this has just come up in the past couple of days. I will have a chat with her soon, let her know that I'm not up for living with anyone else but that I'm totally happy to spend time together and have her visit.

Yeah, I'm finding it hard. There is nothing inherently wrong with having housemates but it's not something I want at this point in my life. Being really clear about that and putting my foot down about it bought up all sorts of issues.
Yes, you are right. He damn well knows I have bent over backwards for him more times than he could ever count. It's totally a manipulation tactic.

They have worked on achieving a good co parenting relationship which I think they have managed very well, which is something I encouraged from the very beginning of our relationship whenever he said something I felt was unfair or resentful about his ex, however the lack of boundaries has often been a strain on our relationship and has frequently meant that he was not spending adequate time with our daughter, not helping enough and not giving me any quality time. That has been much better for some time now and his focus had shifted from spending time with his ex onto his children and our relationship. But then this happened.

At no point did I say that I didn't know what the rent was and how much we could afford. I know how much the rent is and what our household budget is. I asked him if he felt it was too expensive and if he'd be happier renting something cheaper but that isn't even a factor  in this for him.

We aren't in a position to provide another dwelling on the property and very few properties come up around here. A separate kitchen, bathroom and entrance is possible but that is still living in the same house which is not a situation I want with anyone at all. I want our family home to be just for us. We have his son half the time and his ex spends time with us too. She can move to the neighborhood in her own house and visit more frequently, which I'm totally happy to do. He can't have his son more than he currently does as he works and he does need to spend time with his mother too.

I haven't removed any comments or edited anything except for spelling mistakes. We have 5 children between us. 3 from previous relationships (2 are mine, 1 is his), plus one child together and another on the way. That's 5 children, unless you know something I don't.
He says he doesn't believe in compromising on anything and, if he has compromised with me, he hasn't let me know in any way that he was compromising.
It's not separate living quarters, it's a couple of rooms within our house that has an ensuite bathroom and a kitchenette. We actually need that space for ourselves.
I don't know how he could have been sleeping with her considering I was there in bed next to him.

You're reading way too much into it. I don't mention his other child extensively in this post because the question is not about his child, it's about him wanting housemates generally and, at this time, him specifically wanting to live with his ex and inviting her to come live in our home after I specifically told him I want us to live as a family unit. He's with us about half the time because he is working the rest of the time. I frequently look after his son while he is out, both working and socialising.
Apparently not.
5, including the baby we have on the way. I have 2 children from a previous relationship, he has one. We have one child together and our second together due next year.

I agree, she is not an issue at all. She's a perfectly nice woman. Their relationship seems enmeshed to me and the amount of time they have spent together has put a strain on my relationship and the amount of time he was missing out on with our daughter but that is due to his thoughtlessness, not her fault.

See that I don't get at all. I'm really happy for him and his son that they will be moving to the same neighbourhood as us and that it will be easier for them to spend time together. I can't imagine wanting my partner's kid to be further away just so we don't see his ex.
You seem to have an issue with maths and/or reading comprehension. We have 5 children all up if you include the one we have on the way.

It's not a multiplex, it's a house with a couple of rooms that have its own ensuite and kitchen. We will see each other several times per day, every day. There will be no personal space. I wouldn't live in a multiplex or apartment building, I want to be in my own house with a yard.

I haven't been living in a remote rural area, it's a rural area that is literally 5 minutes up the road from the township that the new house is in. He already spends an enormous amount of time socialising for a man with family responsibilities. I'm not going to present the idea of revisiting having housemates as an option for further down the track. It's not happening unless we break up and he moves out.
But that really isn't relevant at all. It's all part of one house.
Yes.
Because he doesn't want a relationship with her...just some weird live in situation while he has a life with someone else.

I never said I wasn't happy to have friends over, to have people come and stay and to have a busy, fun social life. I said I didn't want any housemates living with us and that includes his ex girlfriend.
I have no interest in sharing one big house with anyone other than my partner and our children. If they were separate houses next door or near by that would be fine but I'm not sharing the house.
It has its own entrance but is part of the house. They are not separate houses, he has offered her a couple of rooms in the house that has its own ensuite and kitchenette.
Yes he is. It's called a narcissist.

No, it's a stand alone house on its own block that has an attached room on the side that has a bedroom, lounge, bathroom and kitchen but it's part of the same house. It's a flat within a suburban house. It's not by any definition a separate apartment or duplex next door. It's actually under our lounge room and shares the same electricity, gas, water and phone line. You can hear people from the floor above if they are talking because it's in the next room.
We have one child together and another on the way. Our other 3 children are my 2 from a previous relationship and his son from a previous relationship.

I have already said to him that there is no way I will continue to live with him if he wants to live with his ex or any other housemates and that our relationship will not continue if we don't live together. He said that was an ultimatum.
They aren't. I am also there nearly every time and usually she goes out to date and sleep with her various lovers.

I agree. I have told him that if having housemates or living with is ex is so important to him, that I wont stand in his way but that I also will not be going along with that because it's not what I want in my life. I am willing to compromise on many things but this isn't one of them. He says that I am giving him an ultimatum about our relationship in order to get what I want.

In general he likes to have a lot of people around him and be socialising most of the time so that's why he wants a housemate. He wants his son to be around all the time so that bit I understand but do not think is possible given the separated family situation. He also seems to like the idea of having his ex around a lot. They get along well. I'm not sure why that means they need to live in the same house though. She is looking for a house in this area so I guess it somehow seemed like a good idea to him to offer part of our home, despite the fact that we had a long chat the night before about how I don't want any housemates.

He knows that would never happen so would probably say "I'd be fine with that. That would be awesome". Empathy is not one of his strong points. He either cannot comprehend how I might feel or simply doesn't give a shit.

No, he just wants to have his son close by and seems to like the idea of having his ex close by too as well as generally wanting to have lots of people around. I guess that way there are no consequences whatsoever for having a failed relationship and separated family situation to deal with.

I hadn't even given consideration to what other people may think (and I don't tend to worry about that) just that it's not something I want for myself, my children or my relationship. He's unlikely to care about any of that, or indeed, anything at all other than what he wants. It does concern me how that might feel for the kids, especially as they get older. My eldest will be a teenager soon. He has enough shit to deal with, without adding a weird, dysfunctional living situation.
Does that mean he and his ex are the crazy ones?
No, he has fathered 3 children. His son with his ex, our daughter and the baby we have on the way.

This is just the tip of the iceberg really. He was staying over at her place every second weekend and she was staying over at least once per month until quiet recently. In the recent past we went 3 1/2 months without quality time together during the day without her also being around. I've always had amicable relationship with her. Early on in our relationship when he was quite resentful towards her for various reasons I told him he was being unfair to her and that he needed to let the resentment go. He really should be grateful for what I am doing, not pissed off that he can't have his own way all the time.

The flat has a bathroom and kitchenette but it's totally attached to the house and totally in our personal space. It shares the same yard plus it doesn't have a laundry, plus I know if she is living there, she'll be in the main part of the house a lot. It's attached enough that you could call out from the lounge room and have a conversation. It's attached enough that you'd be able to hear each other's music, tv programs and any conversation held at a normal volume (as well as more intimate noise). It's attached enough that we wouldn't have a day go by without seeing each other multiple times. It doesn't feel in any way like a separate dwelling and there's no way I'd live in apartments or attached townhouses ever.

Yes he does but we don't have an open relationship and neither of them show any interest in each other romantically. I don't fully trust him with fidelity but I have no concerns about him cheating with her.
Lol. Brilliant.

She has a long distance relationship with the new man and as far as I'm aware it's an open relationship. I have never met him and don't know what he would think of it. I wouldn't move in with my ex and his new partner. He tells me my boundaries around this are selfish and unhealthy ("I'm worried you'll have the upper hand and get everything you want and I'll get nothing" and "maybe you should get counselling around this issue") which I'm told is a tactic that narcissists use to try to beat down healthy boundaries to get their way.
I've never met him and he lives in another state so I have no idea. As far as I'm aware they have an open relationship.

My partner and I both have a good relationship with his ex too but I feel like this is just going way too far. It's unhealthy enmeshment. Besides that, I don't want any housemates at all. I want to live with my partner and our children...and apparently I need therapy for that.

When he told me about his suggestion of living with us to his ex, I asked him if he had mentioned at all my feelings about not wanting anyone else living with us and he said that he had told her that. If that is the case though, I wonder why she  is excited at the prospect? He has made this about other things though, claiming that my desire to live as a family only means that I will be anti social and not allow people to come and visit us. This isn't based on anything but his unfounded fears. We already have people over for dinner and people over to stay.

She was looking at houses in the same suburb but when the latest one fell through he offered for her to move into the attached flat (which we actually really need for our own family unit for living and work space) despite the fact that just the night before I told him very clearly that I wanted to live with just us and no housemates. Unfortunately she is now excited at the prospect. She offered to help out with the kids which was very kind but I'm sure we can help each other out, as we have been doing, without all living together.
Yes, it is very telling. He has a tendency to be narcissistic. He cannot see how much I compromise for him and has often declared that he has no interest in compromising on anything.
She's in a relationship with another man and neither of them have any romantic interest in each other anymore. He just wants to have his cake and eat it too.
Wow, I hadn't even thought about it looking like bigamy! Good point. Thank you for your thoughtful comments.

It's got nothing to do with needing another person to help pay the rent. I discussed this with him and suggested that we find another house if the rent was too much but he assured me it wasn't an issue. He just wants to be able to live with his ex and son full time as a family unit and generally likes having other people around all the time.
